meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (French-inspired statutory regime with residual Sharia influence on personal-status matters; unitary national regime, no sub-state corporate law variance)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Egypt–EU Association Agreement establishing a Free Trade Area (in force since 2004)
Bilateral Investment Treaties in force with Germany, the Netherlands, France, the United Kingdom, the United States, China, Kuwait, Saudi Arabia, and the UAE
Network of Double Tax Avoidance Agreements (DTAAs) in force with China, Japan, South Korea, Germany, France, the Netherlands, the United Kingdom, Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, and the UAE

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law No. 80 of 2002 on Anti-Money Laundering (as amended by Laws No. 7 of 2010 and No. 36 of 2014), its Executive Regulations (Prime Ministerial Decree No. 949 of 2003, as amended), and EMLCU directives; Law No. 159 of 1981 on Commercial Companies (as amended) mandating shareholder and beneficial-owner registers for LLCs; GAFI UBO-register filing requirements as a condition to incorporation; and Law No. 72 of 2017 on Investment (negative-list regime) governing committed capital tracking. The competent AML/CFT supervisor is the Egyptian Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Combating Unit (EMLCU) in coordination with the Central Bank of Egypt (CBE) for the banking channel and the Financial Regulatory Authority (FRA) for the non-banking segment.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation, Memorandum and Articles of Association of the ultimate corporate shareholder(s) — clean Company Registry extract (not older than 90 days)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Home-country official company registry (e.g., UK Companies House, HK CR, UAE MOAT, etc., depending on the parent chain)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization — Egypt is not a party to the Hague Apostille Convention of 1961; the document must be apostilled/authenticated in the issuing country, countersigned by the competent local Ministry of Foreign Affairs, then legalized by the Egyptian Embassy/Consulate having jurisdiction; final translation into Arabic by a sworn translator for GAFI filing.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized and legalized General Power of Attorney appointing the local incorporation agent and authorized signatory (bilingual Arabic/English)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign Notary Public in the parent jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization chain (notary → foreign MFA → Egyptian Consulate in issuing country); no apostille route applicable.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board resolution of the foreign parent authorizing incorporation of the Egyptian LLC, capital subscription and appointment of directors
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign corporate parent (certified extract of board minutes)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization by the corporate secretary/foreign notary followed by the same consular legalization chain; certified Arabic translation required.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and passport copies of ultimate beneficial owners and signatories (KYC bundle)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Parent correspondent bank and foreign passport-issuing authorities
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized copies through the consular legalization route; the Arabic translation must be submitted to GAFI and the tax authority upon TIN issuance.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory multi-list screening of all directors, shareholders and UBOs against the consolidated UN Security Council sanctions list (1267/1988), EU consolidated sanctions list, OFAC SDN and sectoral sanctions (relevant for USD wire rails such as Stripe and standard wire transfers), EMLCU national designations, CBE criminal/AML data list, MENAFATF/FATF public statements, and the Egyptian terrorism list issued under Law No. 8 of 2015 (as amended). Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) — including foreign PEPs and former Egyptian senior officials within a five-year cooling-off period — trigger mandatory enhanced due diligence (sources of wealth and funds, senior-management approval, and heightened ongoing monitoring). The screening evidence must be retained for at least five years after business-relationship termination and is subject to EMLCU and CBE on-site inspection.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: GAFI Investor Services digital portal (www.gafi.gov.eg) — Name-Clearance module, cross-indexed against the Ministry of Interior's General Department of Commercial Registries trade-name database and the unified 'Invest in Egypt' gateway (investinegypt.gov.eg).
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The governing statutory name must be expressed in Arabic script; the Latin-script name (e.g., 'Logistics Fleet Dispatch') may be appended as a transliteration provided the transliteration reflects the Arabic name's phonetics and is not a mistransliteration of a prohibited token. The legal-form suffix 'LLC' must appear in Arabic ('شركة ذات مسئولية محدودة' or 'ش.ذ.م.م'). The Arabic name prevails for GAFI, Commercial Registry, tax and banking filings; the English transliteration is used only as a secondary denomination on the certificate of incorporation.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon automated rejection, the applicant files a reconsideration request with GAFI's name-clearance committee within 15 calendar days, attaching ministerial no-objection letters or registered-trademark evidence; GAFI communicates its written decision within 10 working days. A second refusal may be challenged through the investment grievance mechanism under Article 17 of Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 within 30 days of the decision, followed, if necessary, by an annulment lawsuit before the Administrative Court of the Egyptian State Council within 60 days of the grievance outcome. Name reservation is renewable for another 60-day window upon lapse provided the same registration dossier is filed.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Conditional — GAFI and the Commercial Registry require a physical, verifiable registered address evidenced by a certified lease or title deed; a standalone mailbox-style virtual office is de facto rejected (estimated 80% refusal risk). For the Logistics-Tech SaaS segment, GAFI-licensed business centers, government innovation hubs and Suez Canal Economic Zone (SCZONE) addresses are accepted where a named serviced desk and facility access contract is provided; the remote-work reality of the Telematics activity does not waive the physical-address mandate.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (~15% probability of an unannounced postal/on-site verification during the first 18 months). Primary inspection triggers are VAT invoice mismatches, address re-verification during e-TIN issuance, rent-cheque executions, and EMLCU random site checks on AML files; because the target activity is classified 'Low_Risk_Standard', no intrusive supervision is anticipated beyond standard Commercial Registry integrity sweeps.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Egyptian Companies Law No. 159 of 1981 (as amended by Law No. 4 of 2009 and Law No. 17 of 2015), Articles 29-72 governing Limited Liability Companies; Egyptian Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 and GAFI Executive Regulations; Civil Code and Commercial Registration Law No. 34 of 1976
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) - One-Stop Shop for Company Establishment, in coordination with the Commercial Registry Office
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Memorandum of Association and Articles of Association (Aqd Al-Taasis) filed through the GAFI e-establishment portal
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No mandatory statutory minimum paid-up capital for LLCs under Law No. 4 of 2009; issued capital is divided into equal shares. Cash contributions must be deposited into a preliminary blocked bank account opened in the name of the company under formation, and a bank deposit certificate must be submitted to GAFI; in-kind contributions require a certified valuation report.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION - EG_LLC. Adopted by the subscribers on the date of incorporation. Resolved unanimously that: (1) the subscribers listed in the Memorandum of Association hereby subscribe to the entire issued capital, divided into equal shares, and the bank certificate proving deposit of the paid-up capital is approved; (2) the registered office of the Company is established at [address], Cairo, Egypt, where statutory books will be maintained; (3) [Name] is appointed Managing Director, [Name] Chief Financial Officer, and [Name] Compliance Officer, jointly and severally authorized to complete incorporation filings, open bank accounts, and represent the Company before GAFI, the Commercial Registry, and the Egyptian Tax Authority; (4) the Managing Director is authorized to certify copies of this resolution. Approved unanimously.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI One-Stop Shop / Commercial Registry name database
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit up to three proposed trade names for the LLC through the GAFI e-establishment portal. The names must not conflict with existing registered marks or companies and must not contain prohibited expressions. Ensure the corporate suffix 'Limited Liability Company (LLC)' is appended. Upon approval, obtain the official name reservation certificate valid for a stated period.
required_dossiers: Certified copies of founders' national ID or passports
Name reservation application form
Notarized power of attorney if applying via a registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, file a fresh reservation request with alternative names; no formal appeal is necessary as re-submission is expedited through the same portal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Notarization of Memorandum and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public Office (Maktab Al-Shahr Al-Aqari) or certified Egyptian counsel
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a licensed Egyptian lawyer to draft the Memorandum and Articles of Association in Arabic, specifying the company name, registered office address, capital structure, share subscription, management form (managers), and business object covering ISIC 6201 software development and fleet dispatch telematics. All shareholders or their attorney-in-fact must execute the instruments before a notary public, with each page initialed by the notary.
required_dossiers: Executed Memorandum of Association draft
Executed Articles of Association draft
Notarized powers of attorney for all signing representatives
Name reservation certificate
Passport/National ID copies of all shareholders
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary issues a query, the attorney-in-fact may submit a notarial correcting addendum to cure typographical or formal defects; material amendments require a fresh shareholders' meeting and re-execution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Paid-Up Capital Deposit and Bank Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Egyptian licensed bank (preliminary account holding institution)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a preliminary blocked bank account in the name 'EG_LLC (under establishment)' at a licensed Egyptian bank. Deposit the full cash subscription representing the paid-up capital as stated in the Memorandum of Association. Instruct the bank to issue an unconditional capital deposit certificate addressed to GAFI confirming the balance, account currency, and that the account can only be released upon presentation of the final commercial registration certificate.
required_dossiers: Notarized Memorandum and Articles of Association
Name reservation certificate
Passport/National ID copies of all shareholders
Bank account opening application and KYC forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank certificate contains a discrepancy in names or capital amounts, obtain a corrected reissued certificate before submission; an account closure and re-deposit may be required if the account is not maintained in compliance with Central Bank signage rules.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI One-Stop Shop for Company Establishment (online or physical service window)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Compile and submit the complete incorporation file to GAFI, including the notarized Memorandum and Articles, capital deposit certificate, and lease agreement of the intended registered office. Pay the GAFI filing fee, commercial registry fee, and official gazette publication fee. GAFI will issue the incorporation decision and the initial commercial registration certificate and coordinate the issuance of the tax card through the integrated one-stop-shop mechanism.
required_dossiers: Notarized Memorandum and Articles of Association
Capital deposit bank certificate
Registered office lease agreement or title document
Copy of the name reservation certificate
Passport/National ID copies of all shareholders and proposed managers
GAFI prescribed application forms and fee payment receipts
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If GAFI issues a query or administrative stop, respond in writing within thirty days addressing the noted deficiencies; for material objections to the business object, amend the Articles through a supplementary notarial instrument and re-submit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration and Social Insurance Enrollment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) and National Social Insurance Authority (NSIA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon issuance of the commercial registration certificate, complete tax registration to obtain the final Tax Card, register for payroll tax, and register for e-invoicing. Determine VAT registration criteria under the VAT Law relative to the SaaS subscription and wire transfer revenue model. Simultaneously enroll the LLC as an employer with the NSIA within the statutory period for employee social insurance declarations.
required_dossiers: Commercial registration certificate
Tax card application (Form 1)
Memorandum and Articles of Association
Registered office lease
Directors'/managers' passports and employment data for NSIA, as applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax card application is queried, correct and re-submit through the ETA tax identification portal; penalties for late registration are avoidable by prompt remedy within the notice period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Data Protection and Sectoral Registration for Telematics SaaS
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Central Data Protection Office - Ministry of Communications and Information Technology (MCIT)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Because the fleet dispatch SaaS processes personal and geolocation data, register as a data controller with the Central Data Protection Office under Egyptian Data Protection Law No. 151 of 2020. Maintain a data processing register, appoint a data protection officer, and document lawful bases for processing sensitive telematics data. For recurrent interactive dispatch communications, assess whether an additional value-added service notification is required before the National Telecommunications Regulatory Authority (NTRA).
required_dossiers: Data protection registration form
Data processing inventory and data flow map
Privacy policy and lawful-basis documentation
Commercial registration certificate
Appointment letter of data protection officer
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If MCIT issues objections, submit a corrective action plan within the prescribed ninety-day window demonstrating enhanced consent, anonymization, and cross-border transfer safeguards for fleet telematics data.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable - the enterprise is a non-industrial software/telematics SaaS provider; Industrial Development Authority (IDA) manufacturing licensing requirements are not triggered under the investment scope.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not required for the core software activity; the company operates under the general commercial registration and MCIT data protection registration. No operating or manufacturing permit is mandated for server-based dispatch software.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - office and data processing activity with no physical production, chemical handling, or land alteration; no EIA screening or environmental registration is required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable - no wastewater, VOC, or combustion emissions are generated. E-waste from in-country IT equipment must be transferred to a licensed recycler under Waste Management Regulation Law No. 202 of 2020, and any standby diesel generator, if installed, must comply with Law No. 4 of 1994 ambient air limits.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Office premises only: a Fire Safety Certificate from the General Administration of Civil Defense is required for the registered office, including verification of fire extinguishers, evacuation routes, and alarm systems; the workplace must pass the occupational health and safety inspection under Labor Law No. 12 of 2003, covering interior structural load, electrical safety, and emergency signage before employees are stationed at the Cairo premises.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA — El-Maslahah El-Daribeyah); official e-services portal: https://www.eta.gov.eg; e-invoicing/e-receipts portal: https://invoicing.eta.gov.eg
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1 — Incorporate the LLC via the General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) one-stop shop and obtain the Egyptian Commercial Registry extract, with a notarized Arabic-language power of attorney issued to the local manager. Step 2 — Apply to the competent ETA tax district for the tax card (Bitaqa Daribeyya), i.e., the 10-digit unified Tax Identification Number (TIN); this TIN is a precondition for bank accounts, customs, VAT, and payroll filings. Step 3 — Register for VAT under Law 67/2016 via the ETA e-services portal within 30 days of exceeding EGP 500,000 annual taxable turnover, submitting the commercial registry extract, tax card, constitutive documents, board resolution, and head-office/service-agreement evidence. Step 4 — Register as a withholding agent for salary tax and social insurance when Egyptian employees are engaged. Step 5 — For physical fleet-hardware or telematics-device exports, register with the General Organization for Export and Import Control (GOEIC) and obtain the CBE importer/exporter registry code used for ACID customs declarations. ETA processing generally completes within 10–15 business days.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or hybrid-mismatch look-through election exists under Egyptian law; a domestic LLC is always a separate corporate taxpayer subject to CIT at 22.5% on worldwide income (with foreign tax-credit relief) and is a distinct VAT person. Available elections: (i) choose the fiscal year end subject to ETA approval; (ii) voluntary VAT registration below the EGP 500,000 threshold to obtain input-VAT recovery; (iii) elect Investment Law 72/2017 incentives (deduction of up to 30%–50% of investment cost) or the free-zone regime inside the Suez Canal Economic Zone (0% income tax and VAT-neutral treatment for zone-to-zone supplies), such election being made in the GAFI/SCZone setup agreements; (iv) quarterly VAT export-refund cycle election; and (v) annual re-submission of an Egyptian tax-residence certificate issued by the ETA to claim reduced treaty withholding rates on cross-border payments. Hybrid-mismatch rules are not codified and no elective transparency is available for LLCs.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) under Law No. 67 of 2016 and Executive Regulations
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EGP 500,000 of annual taxable supplies of goods and services (mandatory threshold per VAT Law Art. 15); voluntary registration permitted below the threshold, and exporters of services are encouraged to register irrespective of turnover to secure zero-rating and input-VAT refunds
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory near real-time e-invoicing (B2B) and e-receipts (B2C) under ETA Decision No. 369/2020 and the successive phase-in schedules, currently covering essentially all VAT-registered taxpayers including logistics-technology SaaS providers. Invoices are transmitted in JSON/XML to the ETA Electronic Invoicing System (EIS) through ETA-certified middleware or direct REST/SOAP APIs, signed with the taxpayer's ETA digital certificate; the ETA validates each document in near real time and returns an acceptance code plus a unique digital-stamp hash and QR code that must appear on the invoice. Non-compliant issuance invalidates the document for input-VAT deduction and attracts fines of up to EGP 50,000 per invoice, with business-interruption risk for rejected transmissions.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Export of goods and services is zero-rated at 0% VAT under Law 67/2016 and its Executive Regulations. For the logistics-fleet SaaS/telematics scope, the ETA requires: (i) the supplier is a VAT-registered Egyptian entity; (ii) the services are contractually supplied to a non-resident beneficiary located outside Egypt; (iii) the services are effectively consumed offshore, e.g., fleet data processed or utilized abroad — domestic usage by an Egyptian freight operator would disqualify zero-rating; and (iv) the export consideration is received in foreign currency through the Egyptian banking system. Input VAT attributable to zero-rated exports is creditable, and refund claims follow the quarterly ETA export-refund procedure.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD Entry / ACID-linked declaration) — required for physical fleet-hardware and telematics-device exports; for pure SaaS there is no customs entry and the ETA accepts the service-export evidence set instead
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill (or equivalent electronic transport document) evidencing physical export movement where freight equipment is shipped
Inward Remittance Certificate (IRC / bank SWIFT MT103 credit advice) evidencing receipt of export consideration in Egypt
Signed international software/telematics service agreement and commercial invoice naming the non-resident customer and stating that the service is performed and consumed outside Egypt
ETA zero-rating declaration / export-refund statement as filed in the ETA e-services module
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The ETA may reassess export zero-rating claims within the general 5-year limitation period (6 years where fraud or evasion is alleged). Upon disallowance — e.g., evidence that the service was consumed by an Egyptian resident, that the invoice was fictitious, or that FX proceeds were not repatriated through the banking system — the ETA will claw back the 14% VAT that would have been due, plus a delay penalty of 2% per month (capped at 100% of the principal tax), and statutory evasion penalties commonly ranging up to 100% and escalating to 300% of the evaded tax for deliberate fraud, with criminal referral of responsible officers. Failure to repatriate export proceeds within the Central Bank of Egypt deadline (5 months for goods; the 180-day administrative benchmark for services) also exposes the exporter to customs and foreign-exchange sanctions and loss of input-VAT refund carry-forwards. The ETA maintains risk-scoring analytics on digital exporters; missing or irreconcilable IRC/SWIFT documentation is the most common trigger for clawback and frozen refund balances, and the general manager and board members may be held jointly and severally liable for unpaid VAT and penalties.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Egypt (CBE) — the sole regulatory and supervisory authority for foreign exchange, banking, and payment systems under Law No. 194 of 2020; the General Authority for Investment (GAFI) administers investment approvals, and the Financial Regulatory Authority (FRA) supervises non-bank financial services.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Egypt maintains a managed-floating exchange-rate regime and has subscribed to IMF Article VIII, making the Egyptian pound convertible for current international transactions, including export service receipts, dividends, interest, and profit remittance, provided the underlying documents (contract, audited statements, tax clearance, board resolution) are verified by the administering bank. The capital account is open but documented: foreign-direct-equity injection and repatriation must be reported to the CBE through the bank and referenced to the GAFI investment certificate, and banks apply full AML/KYC scrutiny to every conversion. In practice, profit remittance is impeded not by statutory ceilings but by operational hurdles, chiefly delays in obtaining tax clearance, bank-level internal compliance reviews, and the unwillingness of banks to process large conversions during periods of EGP scarcity.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under CBE Law No. 194 of 2020 and CBE board instructions, exporters must repatriate 100% of the invoice value into Egypt through a licensed bank within 30 days of the date of export (date of shipment for goods; date of invoice or client payment in the case of cross-border SaaS/logistics-telematics services). There is no mandatory surrender ratio to Egyptian pounds: since the 2016 float and the 2022-2024 IMF reform sequence, exporters may keep all proceeds in a CBE-licensed foreign-currency account or voluntarily convert them at the interbank market rate. Balances retained abroad (e.g., in offshore EMI wallets) beyond the 30-day window are treated as unrepatriated export proceeds and expose the LLC to fines, customs sanctions, and the denial of future import/export authorisation; free-zone companies and long-term installment contracts require prior CBE approval for deviation.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow (FDI capital deposit) Account; EGP Operational Account; USD/FCY Current Account
EGP Operational Account; USD/FCY Current Account; Capital Deposit Suspense Account for FDI
EGP Operational Account; USD/FCY Operational Account; dedicated Corporate FX and Trade Desk

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Low for any offshore EMI used as the principal treasury rail; Medium only as an ancillary collection gateway. Legal constraints: offshore digital banks and EMIs (e.g., Wise, Airwallex, Mercury, Payoneer) have no licence to operate in Egypt; EGP-denominated accounts, local clearing, or payment-processing to Egyptian counterparties require a CBE licence or a partnership with a licensed Egyptian bank under the CBE Payment Systems regulation (Law 194 of 2020). An LLC may use such EMIs solely to receive hard-currency SaaS subscriptions from foreign clients, but the accumulated balances must be flowed to the Egyptian bank within 30 days to satisfy export-proceeds repatriation, and the account must be declared in the CBE transfer documentation; otherwise, the structure creates an unrepatriated-proceeds exposure.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is mandatory. Egyptian corporate-account onboarding requires at least one managing director/shareholder and all authorised signatories to appear in person at a branch of the chosen bank; remote-only opening is not permitted for a new LLC. The bank conducts a face-to-face KYC interview, verifies original Commercial Registry extraction, tax card, powers of attorney, board resolutions, and proof of address; documents executed outside Egypt must be notarised and apostilled/consular-legalised where applicable, and a local sponsor or resident director may be requested. A video KYC session is admissible only after the in-person branch interview and for ongoing periodic reviews, not as a substitute for the original onboarding.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO opacity: the LLC is controlled by non-resident shareholders through a holding chain, and the bank cannot identify the natural person owning more than 25% of the entity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete chain-of-title diagram; certified register of members and UBO declaration signed by each shareholder; passport copies and proof-of-residence for all natural-person UBOs; articles of association; board resolution identifying the UBO; negative media and sanctions screening report (UN/EU/OFAC) for each UBO; management accounts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-funds insufficiency: the board injects capital in a single large wire from a personal or third-party account rather than from the shareholder's corporate treasury.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Six-to-twelve months of source-account statements; source-of-wealth declaration (sale of shares, salaries, existing business); shareholder loan agreement or equity-subscription agreement; business plan and valuation; capital deposit slip and GAFI receipt; explanatory memo on the SaaS revenue model.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Export-revenue third-party-payment pattern: SaaS subscriptions are paid by dozens of foreign end-customers through aggregators or automatically converted by payment processors, creating saw-tooth inflows and apparent commingling.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Licensed software/telematics subscription agreements; commercial invoices; payment-processor settlement reports (Stripe/BOC) mapping each inflow to a customer; recurring-revenue ledger; export-invoice register; CBE export-form evidence and bank FX credit advices; cloud and vendor contracts substantiating service delivery.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and high-risk-country routing: payments for fleet-telematics services originate from or transit through jurisdictions with sanctions exposure, or from clients in the transport sector subject to OFAC/EU restrictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Per-client and per-transaction sanctions screening output; end-user and beneficial-owner certifications of customers; written compliance memo and decision file; refusal notices for screened-match counterparties; geolocation/IP and vehicle-fleet registration evidence confirming the lawful use of the SaaS platform in non-sanctioned activities.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Lack of real economic footprint: a digital-only business with a flex-space address and no physical staff makes the bank suspect a shell or pass-through entity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Original lease contract registered for commercial-tax purposes; utility bills; employment contracts and payroll records of Egyptian staff; server/hosting logs and data-centre contracts; company tax card and Commercial Registry history; ISO/SOC2 certificates; client call and dispatch-operation records demonstrating real fleet-route optimisation activity.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route the capital injection as a single SWIFT MT103 from the non-resident shareholder's corporate account to the LLC's foreign-currency account at the selected Egyptian bank. The remittance advice must state the CBE balance-of-payments purpose code for inward foreign direct investment (equity in a non-resident-owned Egyptian LLC) and reference the GAFI investment certificate number, the company's Commercial Registry number, and the tax identification number, so that the receiving bank classifies the inflow as capital rather than trade or personal remittance. Before crediting, the bank verifies the board resolution approving the capital increase or subscription, the shareholders' register, the UBO declaration, and the source of funds; after verification, the funds are booked into a capital-deposit suspense account and, upon issuance of the bank's capital certificate in favour of GAFI, are released into the operational account and converted to EGP, if required, at the interbank rate. A confirmation copy of the MT103 and the bank capital certificate must be retained as the statutory evidence for subsequent profit repatriation.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For a logistics-fleet telematics exporter, disbursements are primarily service payments: cloud-hosting infrastructure, subprocessors, international marketing, legal fees, and contractor remuneration. The main rails are SWIFT MT103 (customer credit transfer) and, where the paying bank requires cover, MT202 COV; Commercial Letters of Credit and documentary collections are reserved for physical imports of hardware (e.g., vehicle sensors, servers) and are unsuitable for software services. The bank executes an outbound transfer only when the instruction matches the account mandate, the underlying contract and final invoice are provided, proof of service receipt is attached, a withholding-tax certificate or stamp evidence is given where Egyptian-source income is paid abroad, the ETA corporate-tax clearance is current, and the CBE service-transaction purpose code is reported. To avoid round-tripping red flags, disbursements should be paid from the same licensed bank that receives the export proceeds, never from an unreported offshore EMI balance.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable FX forward with a CBE-licensed bank, limited to documented underlying current or capital transactions, with tenors typically up to 12 months (CBE-authorized forward product; no speculative or naked positions)
Plain-vanilla FX swap with a licensed domestic bank, used for cash-flow hedging of scheduled import payments against export proceeds
Cross-currency swap for a medium-term foreign-currency term facility, authorized by the CBE on a case-by-case basis and appropriate where the LLC borrows in USD against EGP operating cash flow

Offshore Egyptian-pound non-deliverable forward (EGP NDF) available to non-resident counterparties in London or New York; resident Egyptian entities are not permitted to transact NDFs onshore, so this instrument is excluded from the LLC's compliance-used hedging toolkit
FX options: permissible only with prior CBE approval and currently offered only sporadically to non-bank corporates; not part of the standard hedging plan

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return with audited financial statements attached
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 4 months after the end of the fiscal year; for a calendar-year LLC, the return and audited accounts are due by 30 April of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty and delay interest under Unified Tax Law No. 91/2005; ETA may perform a discretionary assessment, initiate enforced collection, and withhold tax clearance certificates until the return is filed.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual shareholder meeting documentation and formal approval of annual financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders' meeting records at the registered office; GAFI inspection on request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the fiscal year-end; resolutions and approval must be recorded in the statutory minute book
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Managers are responsible for convening the annual meeting; failure to approve accounts prevents the completion of a compliant tax filing package and may create personal liability to shareholders; GAFI may treat the company as non-operating.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Commercial registry continuity confirmation and change filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Registry authority operating within the GAFI one-stop-shop
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Commercial registration record renewed before expiry on a five-year cycle; any change in shareholders, managers, or registered office must be notified within 15 days
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance invalidates the commercial registration certificate; GAFI may reject subsequent filings; prolonged inactivity may result in the company being recorded as dormant and ultimately administratively struck off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial ownership and AML register annual confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: GAFI on inspection; Egyptian Financial Intelligence Unit for AML supervision
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Updated continuously and confirmed at the annual shareholders' meeting; every share transfer must be logged in the statutory register at the time of transfer
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: False or omitted UBO particulars are punishable under AML Law No. 80/2002 and its executive regulations by monetary penalties against the LLC and its managers; repeat offences can lead to manager disqualification and company file suspension.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An active Egyptian LLC is required to appoint at least one licensed auditor when it prepares annual financial statements for the corporate tax filing; there is no general revenue or capital threshold exemption in the Companies Law for LLCs, and the ETA expects independent audit coverage for a going-concern entity.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Egyptian Accounting Standards (EAS), aligned with IFRS; statutory books are maintained in EGP and in the Arabic language.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Egypt does not require a separate annual UBO online affirmation for an ordinary LLC; the entity must maintain a complete shareholder and UBO register, update it within 15 days of any transfer, and confirm its accuracy at the annual shareholders' meeting. The manager's signed declaration is placed in the minute book and remains available for GAFI or AML inspection.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Managers/Directors and their appointments/resignations
Minute Book of Shareholder Resolutions and Management Decisions
Share Transfer Register and pledge/charge records
Beneficial Ownership and AML know-your-customer log

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 120 - USD 350 per annum in Cairo for a local registered office and corporate service agent
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 1,200 - USD 3,500 per annum for a certified Egyptian auditor, depending on transaction volume, related-party balances and reporting complexity

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 22.5% on taxable corporate profit (Law No. 91 of 2005, Income Tax Law, Article 48, as amended; uniform rate for Egyptian LLCs and foreign-owned LLCs).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 incentives: deduction of up to 50% of investment costs in eligible sectors/regions; Free Zone entity status exempts qualifying logistics-tech profits with an annual facility fee (1% of value added); accelerated amortization of software and intangible assets; 5% final branch-remittance tax on after-tax profits repatriated by a foreign branch; no general statutory tax holiday for pure-play SaaS operators.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form No. 19 (Bayan 19) - Annual Corporate Income Tax Return, filed electronically through the Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) e-filing portal (https://www.eta.gov.eg); mandatory Transfer Pricing Disclosure Form and Related Party Transaction Schedule submitted as annexes to the same return.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; provisional advance tax is remitted in 12 equal monthly installments during the tax year (based on prior-year declared tax) and credited against the final assessed liability.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Annual return and final tax payment due within 4 months of the close of the tax year; the tax year is generally the calendar year unless an alternative fiscal year is approved by the ETA.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1 - Taxpayer Identification (Tax Card No. / Commercial Registration No.)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter the ETA Tax Card number and Commercial Registration number of the Egyptian LLC as registered.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Egyptian LLC (whether locally owned or 100% foreign-owned) must hold a valid Egyptian Tax Card; non-resident shareholders do not file this form; appoint a resident tax representative if no permanent establishment exists.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Aggregate turnover from SaaS subscriptions, telematics data licensing, fleet dispatch optimization fees, and implementation services, stated net of VAT.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A foreign LLC without a permanent establishment in Egypt is not subject to CIT on software export revenue; a branch reports only Egyptian-source revenue attributable to the permanent establishment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 1b - Cost of Sales / Service Cost
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Direct cloud hosting, bandwidth, developer payroll, third-party telematics hardware, and fleet-dispatch server costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Inter-company costs charged by the foreign parent or affiliates must satisfy the arm's length principle and be supported by contemporaneous invoices and benchmark documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Salaries (subject to payroll tax), rent, utilities, marketing, R&D, software maintenance, depreciation, and statutory provisions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No deduction is allowed for payments to non-resident affiliates unless the applicable 20% royalty/interest withholding tax has been settled and the foreign recipient's Certificate of Tax Residence is on file.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statutory disallowances: 50% of entertainment expenses, taxes paid on behalf of others, penalties, excessive provisions, and financing charges exceeding arm's length limits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Excess management or service fees paid to the foreign head office are non-deductible absent real substance and effective control testing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue less allowable costs and expenses, after mandatory add-backs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A branch computes net Egyptian-source profit attributable to the permanent establishment only; head-office general overhead is allowed only on an apportioned, substantiated basis.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Offset prior-year tax losses available under the 5-year carryforward rule.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Branch losses may be carried forward solely against future Egyptian-source income of the same permanent establishment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable profit after statutory deductions and loss offsets.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Identical computation scope limited to Egyptian-source income attributable to the Egyptian activity.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Apply the statutory headline rate to taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The same 22.5% rate applies to a foreign-owned branch, with the additional 5% branch-remittance tax on after-tax profits transferred abroad.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Credit the 12 monthly provisional installments paid during the tax year plus any prior overpayments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Branches must pay monthly advances based on prior-year Egyptian tax; no credit is allowed for foreign taxes on unrelated non-Egyptian income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final settlement; excess advances are refundable or creditable against future liabilities.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Refunds to non-residents require ETA verification, an audit, and a valid TRC; the 5% remittance tax applies to the profit transfer equivalent.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Annex A - Transfer Pricing Disclosure Form and Related Party Transaction Schedule
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: List all controlled transactions: SaaS reseller arrangements, intercompany royalties, management fees, cloud infrastructure charges, and shareholder loans, with method selection and benchmarking summary.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Mandatory for any cross-border related-party transaction; incomplete filing triggers penalties of 2% of the controlled transaction value and potential TP adjustment.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: fixed administrative fine plus monthly late-payment surcharge of 1.5% of the unpaid tax for each month or part-month of delay; deliberate non-filing or false declaration constitutes tax evasion, punishable by imprisonment (3-5 years) and a fine of at least the evaded tax; late-paid final tax accrues non-deductible default interest.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% final withholding tax on dividends distributed by an Egyptian LLC to non-resident shareholders (Law 91 of 2005, Article 56, as amended); the 5% branch-remittance tax applies separately to foreign branch after-tax profits, not to shareholder dividends.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a reduced DTA rate (commonly 5%-10% on dividends): (1) obtain an official Certificate of Tax Residence (TRC) from the shareholder's home tax authority for the distribution year, with legalization/apostille and Arabic certified translation; (2) submit the ETA Non-Resident Treaty Relief application and Beneficial Ownership declaration identifying the ultimate shareholders; (3) file with the ETA International Taxation Department either before distribution (to authorize reduced withholding at source) or after distribution within the statutory refund window (up to 5 years); (4) the ETA issues a formal exemption or discharge ruling, and the Egyptian LLC then applies the treaty rate. Relief is denied if the recipient lacks beneficial ownership, economic substance, or fails the shareholding and holding-period conditions of the applicable DTA.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties for software, telematics IP, and data licensing paid to non-residents: statutory 20% withholding tax (final), commonly reduced to 10%-15% under active DTAs; interest on shareholder loans and third-party financing paid to non-residents: statutory 20% withholding tax, commonly reduced to 10%-15% under DTAs; no Egyptian WHT on cross-border SaaS export services in the absence of a permanent establishment; thin-capitalization and deemed-dividend rules may re-characterize excessive related-party debt as equity.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File mandatory when annual controlled transactions exceed EGP 15,000,000 for goods/services, EGP 9,000,000 for financial transactions, or EGP 6,000,000 for intangibles/royalties (Ministerial Decree No. 632 of 2021); Master File required when the MNE group's consolidated revenue is at least EGP 10,000,000,000; CbC notification applies to groups with consolidated revenue of EUR 750,000,000 or more; documentation must be contemporaneous and is filed with the annual return, with ETA production demand enforceable within 30 days.
